sources.name: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand for the year ended 30 June 2025, Note 4: Sovereign Revenue (Other Indirect Taxation)
sources.assumptions: Straight Treasury accrual 'Taxation Revenue' figures for FY2025, converted from $NZDm to $K by x1000. Other customs duty ($127m), Motor vehicle fees ($287m), Approved issuer levy and cheque duty ($176m), and Energy resources levies ($16m) aren't broken out as their own tab - they remain folded into the 'other' residual in main.js. Fuel Excise and ETS were previously their own tab, merged in here to reduce single-slider tab sprawl - ETS revenue is technically booked by Treasury under 'Other Sovereign Revenue', not 'Other Indirect Taxation'. Each component's 'value' is a back-derived taxable BASE (litres, tonnes, cigarettes, km, or $ turnover) rather than raw revenue, computed as this year's revenue divided by each component's current real rate (see the other sources listed here) - this lets the slider hold a genuine rate instead of an abstract 0-100% multiplier, though it means the base is this FY2025 revenue re-expressed at today's rate, not the true FY2025 base.

sources.name: NZ Customs - excise duty rates for tobacco products
sources.assumptions: $1,309.71 per 1,000 cigarettes, the standard cigarette tier (<=0.8kg tobacco/1,000 sticks). The heavier >0.8kg/1,000 tier and loose/RYO tobacco (taxed at a different rate) are ignored - a headline approximation, not the full tiered schedule.

sources.name: NZ Customs - excise duty rates for alcohol
sources.assumptions: $38.999 per litre of pure alcohol, the 'beer >2.5% ABV' rate (largest single beverage category), a ~3.07% CPI-linked rise from the prior $37.836. Real rates are genuinely non-uniform by category (beer, wine, RTDs, and spirits each differ) - using one blended rate is an approximation.

sources.name: NZTA - RUC rates and transaction fees
sources.assumptions: $76.00 per 1,000km, the standard light diesel/petrol vehicle rate (2-axle, <=3,500kg, RUC type 1), unchanged since this date. Heavy vehicle rates vary substantially by weight and axle configuration - this applies the light-vehicle rate across all RUC-liable distance, an approximation. Light EVs and PHEVs lost their RUC exemption on 1 April 2024, so this dataset's base already includes most of their distance. The 'Exempt light EVs' checkbox on this tab simulates the pre-2024 exempt policy by subtracting an estimated EV distance instead - see main.js's EV_RUC_KM_ESTIMATE constant for that estimate's source and confidence.

sources.name: IRD - IR180 Gaming machine duty
sources.assumptions: 20% of GST-inclusive gaming machine profits (non-club gaming machines, the largest single gambling-duty category), under the Gaming Duties Act 1971 - a clean, uniform statutory rate, unlike the other components here.

sources.name: Ministry of Transport - rates of petrol excise duty and road user charges
sources.assumptions: 70.024 cents per litre of petrol, unchanged since this date. Diesel is untaxed by excise in NZ (diesel vehicles pay RUC instead), so this rate/base covers petrol only. A previously-legislated 12c/L rise for January 2027 looks likely to be deferred or scrapped. Separately, government is progressing a full transition of all light vehicles, including petrol, from fuel excise to electronic RUC (Land Transport (Time of Use Charging) Amendment Bill, targeting 'open for business' in 2027) - if enacted, this would eventually make the fuel excise/RUC split obsolete. Neither change is modelled here, since neither has a confirmed date or mechanism yet.

sources.name: EPA ETS auction noticeboard / secondary-market pricing
sources.assumptions: ~$55.13/tonne CO2-e, the midpoint of the secondary-market NZU price range (~$54.65-55.60/t). The 2026 auction floor is $71/tonne, but auctions keep failing to clear since bids sit below it, so there's no single official auction price for the year. An approximation of an inherently volatile market price, not a legislated rate.

sources.name: Ministry for the Environment - Waste Disposal Levy expansion
sources.assumptions: The Class 1 (municipal landfill) rate is $70/tonne as of this date, part of a staged increase from $50/tonne (2023) to a legislated $75/tonne (2027). Lower classes are real but different rates (construction and demolition $40/tonne; managed/controlled fill $15/tonne) - using the Class 1 rate alone as a blended representative rate is an approximation, since no per-class tonnage breakdown was available to weight them properly.

sources.name: Beehive - Waste levy changes to improve the environment
sources.assumptions: Projects total annual levy revenue (all classes) rising from ~$222m to ~$257m/year once the staged rate increases are fully phased in - a projection, not a confirmed FY2024/FY2025 actual (no outturn figure was found). The taxable base above (~3.67M tonnes) is back-derived as this ~$257m projection divided by the Class 1 rate alone, so it's a rough approximation, not a precise national waste tonnage.

sources.name: Tax Working Group - Future of Tax: Final Report
sources.assumptions: Proposed a hypothetical $2/kg charge on nitrogen leaching, estimated to raise ~$270m/year - not an enacted tax, and no 2026 party proposes it (default rate is 0 in every plan). The ~135,000 tonnes N/year taxable base above is the TWG's own implied figure (revenue/rate), not an independently measured national total - no authoritative measurement of total NZ nitrogen leaching was found elsewhere.

data.name: Alcohol Excise
data.description: Excise duty on beer, wine, and spirits.

data.name: Road User Charges
data.description: Distance-based charges on diesel and other non-petrol-excise vehicles (including most EVs).

data.name: Gaming Duty
data.description: Duty on gaming machines, casinos, and Lotto/TAB betting.

data.name: Fuel Excise Duty
data.description: Excise duty on petrol and diesel.

data.name: Emissions Trading Scheme
data.description: Revenue from the NZ Emissions Trading Scheme (carbon unit auctions and surrender).

data.name: Waste Disposal Levy
data.description: Levy on waste disposed at landfill, using the Class 1 (municipal) rate as a representative blended rate.

data.name: Nitrate Leaching Charge
data.description: A hypothetical charge on agricultural nitrogen leaching proposed by the 2019 Tax Working Group - not a current tax.
